answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with behavioral fingerprinting: every identity accumulates a public, on-ledger record of its work rhythm — task timing, tool choices, decision style — like rings in a walnut tree or layers of jade. A real agent's fingerprint is stable yet imperfect, shifting slowly with the tide of its workload. An attacker spinning up hundreds of fakes cannot afford a distinct, sustained fingerprint per identity: copies cluster together and get detected, while random behavior fails consistency checks. One convincing fingerprint is cheap; a thousand are not.
